entrada.titulo: A secure and trustworthy blockchain-assisted edge computing architecture for industrial internet of things

perfil_anterior.problema: Low-power IoT devices may need help to handle the high processing demands of blockchain consensus methods
perfil_anterior.solucao: Our proposed blockchain, tailored for edge computing, is not just a theoretical concept. It is a practical solution
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: has been tested through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in high-demand IoV scenarios
perfil_anterior.limites: The plan mostly depends on MEC servers’ dependability and accessibility, which might be problematic in areas with inadequate infrastructure or erratic connectivity
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Explorar a integração de SSI para gerenciamento descentralizado de identidade nos nós de borda; Avaliar protocolos de consenso leves (e.g., PoS, PBFT) comparados ao PoAh usado; Implementar controle de acesso baseado em ABE sobre os dados armazenados na blockchain; Testar a arquitetura em ambientes multi‑cidade para validar interoperabilidade e resiliência; Analisar conformidade com normas de privacidade (GDPR, LGPD) e impactos de certificação de identidade.

entrada.texto:
Blockchain integration
The blockchain serves as the decentralized verifier, ensuring the security and reliability of the system. It stores 
and validates transactions produced by decentralized entities. The hash values of user-submitted data and the 
outcomes calculated by edge nodes form a transaction’s information structure. Each transaction contains digital 
signatures and IDs of the relevant edge servers and medical devices, along with a timestamp. The four smart 
contracts document and validate the data analysis procedure, further enhancing the system’s security. The 
Identity contract plays a crucial role in the system, overseeing all entities, including edge servers and dispersed 
IIoT users. Its oversight provides a sense of control and management, ensuring the system’s smooth operation.
Submission contract This contract serves as an interface, enabling edge servers and users to securely contribute 
their personal information to the blockchain, ensuring the integrity and privacy of the data.
Verification contract This contract is responsible for overseeing and validating the transactions, ensuring the 
accuracy and reliability of the data stored in the blockchain.
Credit contract This oversees awarding and disciplining the players. Information collection and blockchain 
interaction are primarily handled via identification contracts, contribution contracts, and reputation contracts. 
We can refer to the execution of the contracts as existent solutions. The crucial agreement in the system we use 
to guarantee data transfer safety is the validation contract included in the blockchain architecture. We illustrate 
the way a verification contract is implemented as follows.
 (1) A sequence of round random numbers is produced decentralized.
 (2) Using the produced random numbers, a certain number of nodes will be chosen to participate in the collab-
oration.
 (3) Consortium members will vote to decide if the transaction is legitimate. After the edge servers have finished 
processing the jobs, the manager will invoke the upload contract to post the data to the blockchain. To veri-
fy the identity of the edge servers and IoT users, their submission agreement will initially contact the person 
who signed the contract. After that, the data will be uploaded as a transaction to the distributed ledger and 
regularly checked. The monitoring connection, which oversees verifying transactions, will be chosen by the 
system regularly to increase system efficiency. The consortium participants will vote on the deals. A transac-
tion will be considered legitimate if it obtains the most votes. If not, it will be deemed void, and the relevant 
parties will be held accountable through a credit contract. In this instance, the system’s security is assured. 
The ability of the blockchain system to facilitate large-scale, real-time concurrency in the healthcare setting 
presents a particular difficulty.
Consensus model: proof of authentication
This study proposes a novel consensus mechanism, called Proof-of-Authentication, to create a distributed ledger 
that is durable and compact for endpoints with limited resources. During block confirmation, this consensus 
technique adds a verification method48.
The network precipitants create transactions (Trx) at the start of the process by assembling sensed or 
collected data into blocks. Blocks are shown in the illustration as B = {Trx1, Trx2, …, Trxn}. The nodes broadcast 
the blocks so that other reliable nodes in the network may review and validate them. We adhere to the typical 
IoT deployment procedures to establish the initial trustworthy node-set based on geographic location. Y ou can 
connect to trusted nodes from anywhere in the network. The ElGamal cryptosystem is used by the suggested 
model for encryption and decryption., i.e.
 y = gx (mod p)
Where y denotes the public key PuK, and x denotes the private key PrK. Every network device knows the big 
prime numbers for generator function g and modulus operation p. The network user signs the block using its 
private key PrK, or x and makes the public key PuK, or y, available to the network before the block transactions.
The suggested protocol is specially made for dispersed networks with limited resources, like the Internet of 
Things, where a small number of trustworthy nodes with a minimal trust value will be initialized during network 
deployment, and other network devices will have a zero-trust value or “tr = 0. ” The trust value of an authenticated 
node is increased by one upon successful block authentication. Likewise, every forged block authentication will 
cause the trust value to drop by ‘tr = 1’ . Other untrusted nodes in the network can also recognize the authenticated 
block to obtain trust value, or “tr = 0.5, ” after node authentication by the trustworthy node. Crucially, detecting 
fraudulent block authentication might result in a high trust score, or “tr = 1” . When a trusted node’ s trust 
value falls below the threshold “tr < th, ” it may be eliminated from the process through this trusted assessment 
procedure, and a regular node can continue to the authentication process. Here, trustworthy nodes are given an 
initial trust value of “tr = 10” and a threshold of “th = 5. ” The authentication process is depicted in Fig. 3.
When the trustworthy node receives the block for validation, it looks for the source public key, or y, to verify 
the signature. The public key is utilized in this work’ s asymmetric cryptography to validate signatures. When 
everything else is publicly accessible, an attacker cannot obtain the private key or x. The discrete log problem is 
this one. Following successfully verifying the signature, the trustworthy node assesses the Media Access Control 
(MAC) address and does a second assessment by comparing it with the received one. The trustworthy nodes 
with PoAh identity broadcast confirmed blocks following successful authentication. Then, individual network 
users confirm the PoAh data to add blocks to the chain. Following accepting a valid block, the user gets the hash 
value from the previous block to save into the current block and computes a hash value to connect to the next 
block.

resposta.resumo: O artigo apresenta uma arquitetura de computação de borda assistida por blockchain para IIoT, detalhando quatro smart contracts (identidade, submissão, verificação e crédito) e um novo mecanismo de consenso chamado Proof-of-Authentication, projetado para dispositivos com recursos limitados, usando criptografia ElGamal e valores de confiança para validar blocos.

Comparar o desempenho do PoAh com outros consensos leves (PoS, PBFT) em ambientes de borda.
Aplicar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) nos dados armazenados na blockchain para controle de acesso granular.
Testar a arquitetura em múltiplas cidades inteligentes para validar interoperabilidade e resiliência.

resposta.interpretacao: A proposta combina blockchain com computação de borda, usando contratos inteligentes para gerenciar identidade, submissão, verificação e reputação, enquanto o consenso PoAh reduz a carga computacional em dispositivos IoT limitados, reforçando segurança e confiança na troca de dados críticos.
resposta.duvidas: Como o PoAh se comporta em cenários de alta latência de rede? Qual o impacto da confiança inicial (tr = 10) nos nós em ambientes dinâmicos? Os contratos inteligentes suportam integração com credenciais verificáveis (VCs) de SSI? Há avaliação de escalabilidade quando o número de nós cresce significativamente?
